title: Polga 2004: thoracic IDP (mid and lower), 30 deg axial rotation (left)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute in vivo thoracic intradiscal pressure (MPa), mean of the volunteers measured at that level group; min/max = range of the individual values

source.authors: Polga DJ, Beaubien BP, Kallemeier PM, Schellhas KP, Lew WD, Buttermann GR, Wood KB
source.sample: 6 subjects (4M, 2F); 6 healthy adult volunteers, mid (T6-T7 or T7-T8) and lower (T9-T10 or T10-T11) thoracic discs

protocol.summary: Needle pressure transducer in mid (T6-T7 or T7-T8) and lower (T9-T10 or T10-T11) thoracic discs of 6 volunteers; standing postures and hand loads. Level and needle orientation had no significant effect; highest pressure holding 10 kg in each hand (abstract via Ghezelbash lab validation targets).
how_to_simulate: Scale the model to the Polga subject (protocol.subject_model: male, 28 y, 178 cm, 73 kg; Polga Methods)
Posture: standing, 30 deg axial rotation to the left (17% lumbar / 83% thoracic, Bruno 2015; Ghezelbash lab posture library 12)
Output: compression F and flexion th at T6-T7 and T7-T8 (average -> 'mid') and at T9-T10 and T10-T11 (average -> 'lower')
Convert with Ghezelbash 2016 Eq. 6 applied unchanged: P = F / A, A = 663 mm2 (mid) / 897 mm2 (lower) (Kishimoto 2016 CT areas, sex-weighted); compare with data[].mean and range

subject_model.source: Polga 2004 Methods (primary): 4 men, 2 women, mean age 28 y (19-47), 73 kg (54-81), 178 cm (163-191), BMI 22.8.
subject_model.disc_area_source: Ghezelbash lab validation targets (subjects.polga): in vivo CT vertebral endplate CSA of Kishimoto et al. 2016 J Orthop Res 34:1418 as used for Polga's data by Schmid et al. 2020 J Biomech 99:109536: T7-8 7.1 / 5.7 cm2 (M/F), T10-11 9.6 / 7.7 cm2, weighted 4 M : 2 F -> mid 6.63 cm2, lower 8.97 cm2. Bruno 2015 instead measured vertebral CSA on their own CT of matched subjects (values not tabulated).

protocol.idp_conversion: IDP = -1.556e-2 + 1.255 P + 1.243e-2 th + 3.988e-2 P^2 - 1.212e-2 P th + 1.669e-3 th^2 (MPa), P = F_compression / A_disc (MPa = N/mm2), th = L4-L5 intersegmental flexion from upright standing (deg, + flexion). Source: Ghezelbash et al. 2016 Biomech Model Mechanobiol 15:1699, Eq. 6 (U01 p.10; quadratic fit to the Shirazi-Adl 2006 L4-L5 FE model, R2 0.999, RMSE 0.025 MPa; derived with that model's disc area 1455 mm2, applied with the subject's own area); used again as Eq. 1-2 in Ghezelbash et al. 2020 J Biomech 102:109550 and in the Ghezelbash lab MSK validation. Sensitivity alternative: classical Nachemson factor IDP = F / (0.66 A) (Bruno et al. 2015 J Biomech Eng Eq. 2; Dreischarf 2016 V05 uses F = 0.66 IDP A). For thoracic discs no thoracic-specific relation exists; the Ghezelbash lab validation applies Eq. 6 unchanged with th = the segment's flexion (Bruno 2015 and Schmid 2020 likewise applied the lumbar factor).
protocol.notes: Thoracic discs show ~0.2-0.3 MPa even prone/unloaded (Polga 2004 via Wilke 2020, MSK_VALIDATION.md), which compression-based models do not reproduce. Level groups: mid = T6-T7 or T7-T8; lower = T9-T10 or T10-T11 (each volunteer measured at one disc per group).
protocol.posture_note: Flexion/extension set with a pendulum inclinometer (to 30 deg flexion, 15 deg extension); twisting and lateral bending to the maximum comfortable limit (lateral bending angle not reported).

extraction.from: Polga DJ et al. Spine 2004;29:1320-1324, Table 1
extraction.check_notes: Checked against the primary paper (Polga 2004 Spine 29:1320, Table 1) on 2026-11-12. Polga 2004 Table 1 (primary): mean +/- SE (range). n = discs measured: mid 5 (4 T6-T7, 1 T7-T8), lower 7 (5 T9-T10, 2 T10-T11) from 6 volunteers (Methods). SD = SE x sqrt(n) assuming the SE is over these discs. Earlier values were digitised from Schmid 2020 (via the Ghezelbash lab targets); changed [1.11, 1.01] -> [1.11, 1.02].

pass_rule.rule: per task: model inside the measured range (min-max of the 6 volunteers) or within 0.26 x measured; pooled Polga tasks: Pearson r >= 0.80 and regression slope 95% CI contains 1
pass_rule.source: Ghezelbash lab validation targets tolerance_policy.idp_thoracic_aggregate (Bruno 2015 obtained r = 0.87, slope CI 0.99-1.97)
